name: Sian Ka'an Biosphere Reserve
blurb: Seagrass, mangroves and reef on the Yucatan coast, ruled by crocodiles and jaguars.

tip.title: Strip the seagrass
tip.text: Seagrass beds feed manatees, green turtles and urchins and shelter young lobsters. Remove Turtle grass and watch the grazers and the crocodile and jaguar above them feel it.

notes: The species list comes from GBIF occurrence records inside a circle around the park, so it can include nearby areas. Feeding links come from GloBI records and the sources listed where they state them; others are general ecology and are illustrative.

nodes.desc: Seagrass that carpets shallow lagoons and the reef back-waters. Larval spiny lobsters settle in these beds, and manatees and green turtles graze them.
Salt-tolerant trees along the coast and lagoons. Their roots shelter young marine animals and their leaves are eaten by manatees.
A common tropical forest tree. GloBI records many birds, bats and a monkey eating its fruit.
A grazing urchin of reefs and seagrass beds. Spiny lobsters eat sea urchins.

nodes.name: Green turtle
nodes.desc: Adults mostly graze seagrasses and algae in shallow lagoons. Large sharks and, on land, jaguars can take them.
A large grazer eating many aquatic plants, mainly seagrass, plus mangrove leaves at high tide. It has almost no natural predators.
A forest rodent that eats fruit and seeds and buries some of them, helping trees spread. Jaguars and boas prey on agoutis.
A fruit-eating canopy primate. GloBI records it eating gumbo-limbo and palm fruit.
A fruit-eating bat that carries seeds around the forest. Boas are recorded eating it.
Nursery in seagrass and mangrove, adult on reefs. It eats molluscs, urchins and other bottom animals, and is eaten by groupers and sharks.
A plunge-diving seabird of the coast that eats fish such as mullet. Turkey vultures are recorded eating pelicans.

nodes.name: Turkey vulture
nodes.desc: A scavenger that cleans up carcasses. GloBI records it eating manatee, pelican, gray fox and boa.
An omnivorous canid that eats fruit and small animals. GloBI records it eating gumbo-limbo fruit and boas eating it.
An apex predator of mangrove lagoons. Adults eat fish, birds, mammals and turtles, and in Quintana Roo fish make up most identified prey.
The top land predator. It ambushes mammals such as agoutis and can also take turtles; Yucatan forests are fragmented by roads and development.
Strong tropical light drives growth of seagrass, mangroves and forest.
Break down fallen leaves, mangrove litter and carcasses, returning nutrients to the soil.
